NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's web site under City Council Meeting agendas at www.RollingHillsEstates.gov and
  during regular business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's web
  site and a recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP -TV
  Channel 35 (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome on any item during City Council consideration of the item. An opportunity is
  also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If you would like to
  address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public comment, please
  complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JANUARY 14, 2025

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR STEGURA called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Mark Waronek, Mayor of the City of Lomita.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Attorney Steve McEwen
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson
  Senior Accountant Fernando Estrada

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING JANUARY  27,  2025  AS  INTERNATIONAL
  HOLOCAUST REMEMBRANCE DAY

MAYOR STEGURA declared January 27, 2025, as International Holocaust Remembrance
Day.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

MAYOR STEGURA removed item 5G from the Consent agenda which contained the incorrect
attachment.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-F, 5H-J AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF DECEMBER 2024 & JANUARY 2025

  APPROVED WARRANTS 68059 THROUGH 68143 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $806,554.59 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 120324 THROUGH
  120524; 010125 THROUGH 010325; IN THE AMOUNT OF $274,667.95 FOR
  A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $1,081,222.54 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JANUARY 14, 2025
 C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF NOVEMBER 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF NOVEMBER 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  BUDGET AMENDMENTS FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025

  APPROVED THE BUDGET AMENDMENTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025.

F.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF DECEMBER 2, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF DECEMBER 17, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

I.  COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE 2024 ATTENDANCE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

J.  2024 BIANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT, JUNE 1, 2024 TO DECEMBER
  31, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Los Angeles County Fire Department Assistant Chief Brian Kane provided a community update
as it relates to the recent Palisades and Eaton Fires, and dangerous wildfire weather
conditions. Chief Kane also discussed fire response and readiness on the Peninsula and the
redundancies that are in place for resources and communication.

A.  2024 MUNICIPAL INFORMATION SYSTEMS ASSOCIATION OF CALIFORNIA
  (MISAC) EXCELLENCE IN INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY - PRESENTATION BY
  RICH CASTILLION

Rich Castillion presented the City of Rolling Hills Estates with the 2024 Municipal Information
Systems Association of California (MISAC) Excellence in Information Technology Award.

B.  SOUTH COAST BOTANIC GARDEN'S INTERIM CHIEF OPERATING OFFICER,
  KATRYN HEISE - UPCOMING PROJECTS

Mark Waronek, Vice President of the South Coast Botanic Garden Board of Directors and
Mayor of Lomita, introduced Interim Chief Operating Officer Katryn Heise, who announced
upcoming programs and events coming this spring to the South Coast Botanic Garden.

Executive Director of Peninsula Friends of the Library Merlin David announced upcoming
events.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  RESOLUTION NO. 2593 APPROVING THE PROPOSED USE OF FISCAL YEAR
  2025-26 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the Public Hearing; 2) Receive any
  public testimony; 3) Close the Public Hearing; and, 4) Waive further reading and
  approve Resolution No. 2593 authorizing execution of a contract with the Los Angeles
  County Community Development Commission for participation in the program for
  funding of the ADA Access Ramp and Sidewalk Improvement Program as identified

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JANUARY 14, 2025
   in the Program and Conditions Assessment Report dated April 2, 2014 in the amount
  of $21,773.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

Director Wahba explained that the ADA Access Ramp and Sidewalk Improvement Program
is a 14-year program, in response to MAYOR STEGURA.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2593 AUTHORIZING EXECUTION OF A
  CONTRACT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION FOR PARTICIPATION IN THE PROGRAM
  FOR FUNDING OF THE ADA ACCESS RAMP AND SIDEWALK
  IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM AS IDENTIFIED IN THE PROGRAM AND
  CONDITIONS ASSESSMENT REPORT DATED APRIL 2, 2014 IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $21,773.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2593 by title.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  ANNUAL COMPREHENSIVE FINANCIAL REPORT FOR FISCAL YEAR ENDED
  JUNE 30, 2024

  Recommendation: That the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates receive
  and file Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) for fiscal year ended June
  30, 2024.

Senior Accountant Estrada provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), and
introduced Demi Hite, CPA, Senior Auditor with Rogers, Anderson, Malody & Scott, who
presented a summary of the FY 2024-2025 audit.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE THE ANNUAL COMPREHENSIVE FINANCIAL REPORT
  (ACFR) FOR FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE 30, 2024.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO ADJOURN TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD
  MEETING.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JANUARY 14, 2025
 **ADJOURN TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD MEETING**

B.  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ANNUAL BOARD OF DIRECTORS MEETING

  Recommendation: That the Rolling Hills Estates Pepper Tree Foundation Board of
  Directors receive and file this report.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Supervisor Pinuelas provided an update on the fundraising campaign, noting that staff has
been actively developing materials and establishing preliminary connections with
prospective large donors, in response to BOARD MEMBER HUFF.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  VICE CHAIR ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by BOARD MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

  BOARD MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by BOARD MEMBER HUFF, TO
  RECONVENE THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING.

**RECONVENE CITY COUNCIL MEETING**

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  QUARTERLY WORK PLAN UPDATE

  Recommendation: Receive and file.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

City Manager Grammer explained the purpose and goals of the Multi-jurisdictional Hazard
Mitigation Plan, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

There being no objection, MAYOR STEGURA so ordered.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the Steering Committee meeting for the South Bay Cities
Council of Governments (SBCCOG) and plans to attend the City Selection Committee meeting
on January 21.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JANUARY 14, 2025
 12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  2025 CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council review and discuss the proposed
  Council/Committee assignments and approve as presented.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded  by  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  APPROVE AS PRESENTED.

B.  COMMISSION/COMMITTEE APPOINTMENTS AND RE-APPOINTMENTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council reappoint the current Commission and
  Committee members and make appointments to fill the vacancies on the Traffic and
  Safety Committee and Environmental Advisory Committee from the recently
  interviewed candidates.

City Clerk Pettit provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  REAPPOINT CURRENT COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE MEMBERS.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

It was the consensus of the Council that all of the candidates were excellent, thanked them all
for their willingness to serve the City, and encouraged them all to remain engaged and reapply
if they are not appointed to a Committee.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPOINT LYLE HALL AND TALEEN TERTZAKIAN TO THE TRAFFIC &
  SAFETY COMMITTEE.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPOINT JEFFREY MCBURNEY AND  ANDY  REIN  TO  THE
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:44 p.m. MAYOR STEGURA adjourned the meeting in memory of those who lost their
lives and homes in the recent Palisades and Eaton fires, as well as in memory of former
President Jimmy Carter. The meeting was adjourned to Tuesday, January 28, 2025, at 7:00
p.m. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

  [signatures on following page]

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JANUARY 14, 2025
 Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Debby Stegura, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
JANUARY 14, 2025
